name: Wilderness
overview: The wilderness in Scripture is depicted as a place of both physical desolation and divine encounter. It is where God meets His people, as seen when He found Hagar and her son by a fountain (Genesis 16:7) and led Israel as the 'apple of his eye' through a waste howling wilderness (Deuteronomy 32:10). The wilderness also symbolizes the sinner's state of wandering and need for God's guidance, and it serves as the setting for Jesus' temptation, underscoring its role as a place of testing and dependence on God. Yet, God promises provision and peace even there, making a way and rivers in the desert (Isaiah 43:19) and causing His people to dwell safely (Ezekiel 34:25).
